About Ayo

We are a venture-backed early-stage startup developing processors specialized for machine learning. The processor will provide orders of magnitude improvement in speed and power efficiency with a goal of unseating the GPU as the dominant computing platform for machine learning.

The Role

We're looking for a hands-on machine learning engineer to join our founding team and get models running on our photonic processor. You'll take models from PyTorch to prototype silicon and digital twins, figure out what breaks, fix it, and feed what you learn straight back to the hardware team. This is a builder role: you'll own real problems end to end, move fast, and work shoulder to shoulder with photonics, ASIC, and FPGA engineers who are building something no one has built before.

No prior hardware experience required. If you're early in your career, fresh out of a PhD, and itching to work on something genuinely new, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Partner with our engineering teams to train models that run successfully on Ayo chips

Deploy and run trained models on our prototype hardware and digital twins, and turn them into working demonstrations on our chips

Build and adapt training and inference pipelines for a compute environment that doesn't behave like a GPU

Work directly with hardware engineers to test ideas, find bottlenecks, and shape the processor architecture with what you learn

Build the tooling, benchmarks, and software infrastructure our machine learning work runs on

Help show the world what Ayo's processor can do by supporting demos and go-to-market work

What We're Looking For

PhD or MS in machine learning, computer science, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field (recent grads welcome), or equivalent hands-on experience

Has built and trained neural networks from scratch, and understands how they work under the hood

Full-stack ML engineering skills: data pipelines, training, evaluation, and deployment

Fluent in Python and PyTorch (TensorFlow or JAX also welcome)

A bias toward action: you'd rather ship a working prototype than perfect a plan

Excitement about novel hardware. You don't need photonics or silicon experience, just curiosity and the drive to learn fast

Nice to Have

Experience with distributed training or large-scale compute

Model optimization experience such as quantization, pruning, compilers, or custom kernels (CUDA, Triton)

Interpretability or explainability work

Any exposure to hardware, FPGAs, or analog or in-memory compute

Why Ayo

You'll be a founding machine learning team member, shaping how we deploy machine learning on an entirely new kind of processor.

We are working on a genuinely hard and interesting problem: unseating the GPU as the dominant machine learning compute platform.

Early-stage means real ownership, real impact, and meaningful equity.

Competitive salary. Equity commensurate with stage and seniority. Benefits package including health, dental, and vision.

Fully onsite in Boston - we are a collaborative, in-person team.
